source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Steam sterilization uses saturated steam under pressure for a specified time and temperature to destroy microorganisms, including resistant spores.","B":"Steam sterilization relies mainly on prolonged dry room-temperature air exposure, which gradually removes microorganisms from instrument surfaces.","C":"Steam sterilization uses a brief cold-water rinse followed by air drying, which eliminates microorganisms without requiring pressure or heat.","D":"Steam sterilization depends primarily on ultraviolet light exposure at room pressure, which reliably penetrates wrapped instruments and kills spores."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC describes steam sterilization as exposure to saturated steam under pressure at the required temperature for the required time, and notes that the process is sporicidal. Option A matches those parameters. Option B describes room-temperature drying rather than sterilization. Option C omits the heat and pressure required for an autoclave. Option D substitutes ultraviolet exposure for the steam, pressure, temperature, and time used in steam sterilization.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Disinfection and Sterilization — Steam Sterilization, Overview/Basic Principle: direct contact with saturated steam under pressure at required temperature for specified time; steam sterilization is microbicidal and sporicidal. Current CDC steam-sterilization guidance at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15.
